description: Append-oriented empirical history of HumanityAI operational system-design experiments and changes. This file records observed outcomes and interpretations but grants no authority and cannot override protected governance, security, licensing, constitutional, scheduler, or permission boundaries.

records.problem_trigger: Recent adaptive slots produced substantial repository activity but comparatively low decision progress, with overlapping allocation and verification responsibilities and repeated baseline/brief/candidate-verification cycles.
records.prior_design: Peer-like adaptive workers independently selected high-value safe work, with multiple workers able to research, verify, synthesize, and redirect priorities. Independent Audit existed, but ordinary management/integration ownership was diffuse.
records.hypothesis_rationale: Separating ordinary management from first-line production, second-line verification, and third-line assurance should reduce duplicated compute, increase decision delta per slot, preserve verifier independence, and make integration responsibility explicit without expanding authority.
records.exact_change: Transitioned ordinary operations toward Human/constitution -> Controller D -> Operators A/B -> independent Verifier C -> independent Audit. D owns portfolio allocation, routine internal integration, design memory, and GitLab mirror maintenance. A biases toward direct progress; B preserves exploration; C independently challenges Tier-2 A/B work; Audit remains independent assurance. Introduced risk-tiered integration and a durable portfolio state in agent/portfolio.json.
records.decision_delta_metric: A slot is high-yield when it changes a belief, decision, capability, ranking, uncertainty estimate, adoption judgment, measurable outcome model, or future compute allocation. Repository growth and commit count are not success metrics.

risk_tiered_integration.tier_1: Routine reversible unprotected housekeeping/tooling; exact-head CI required; C optional; D integrates.
risk_tiered_integration.tier_2: Substantive A/B evidence, prioritization, registry, analytical/code, or decision products; exact-head CI plus independent C verdict required before D integration.
risk_tiered_integration.tier_3: Protected/security/governance/licensing/constitutional/agent-authority changes, external PRs, unresolved injection/provenance compromise, or consequential external action; human review required.

expected_benefit: Higher decision delta per unit of scheduled compute.
risks: D could become an allocation bottleneck.
evaluation_criteria: Material decision delta and safe throughput.
lessons: Do not declare hierarchy proven early.

records.prior_design: DH0001 had a C QUALIFY block but no completed integration cycle.
records.hypothesis_rationale: Independent PASS plus exact-head CI should permit safe D integration.
records.exact_change: PR #84 completed producer-C-D cycle under existing authority.

observed_outcomes.observation: PR #84 integrated after C PASS and exact-head CI.

records.problem_trigger: Audit finding #111 and subsequent controller runs exposed stale assignments, duplicates, freshness rework and queue aging.
records.prior_design: Durable portfolio without mandatory post-integration coherence gate or explicit hard WIP limit.
records.hypothesis_rationale: Finish-before-start, WIP<=2, coherence reconciliation, explicit assignment contracts and aging/toil triggers should reduce stale/duplicate execution.
records.exact_change: Adopted human-approved controller-coherence gate and Audit #111 flow standard within ordinary authority.
evaluation_criteria: Aging acted on after >2 healthy cycles.

observed_outcomes.observation: Controller repeatedly held replacement Tier-2 production while queues were congested.

lessons: Keep bookkeeping small and tied to allocation changes.

records.problem_trigger: The bounded P05 Tier-2 assignment released by PR #131 remained non-materialized across more than two healthy controller cycles, leaving no producer-ready candidate while durable state continued to reference the assignment.
records.prior_design: D could release one bounded assignment after clearing WIP, relying on A/B to materialize the assignment into a visible candidate; aging rules required action after two healthy D cycles but there was no evidence that an assignment invisible to the PR queue would self-correct.
records.hypothesis_rationale: Treating non-materialized assignments as failed work pulls—not as invitations to silently reissue or add coordination—should prevent invisible WIP and repeated idle allocation. The smallest simplification is to require the next Tier-2 pull to be one visible bounded candidate at a time, and to return to read-only work if it does not materialize within the existing aging window.
records.exact_change: No authority or scheduler change. New Tier-2 production remains held. This checkpoint records the P05 non-materialization as a process failure and establishes an ordinary-management lesson for the next allocation: release at most one bounded candidate after a fresh coherence check; do not silently duplicate/reissue an invisible assignment; if no producer-ready candidate appears within two healthy D cycles, cancel that pull and reconsider the decision question rather than adding coordination layers.
expected_benefit: Reduce repeated assignment churn and controller toil.
Make producer-ready -> C -> D aging observable from live state.
risks: Cancelling a slow but valuable assignment after two healthy cycles may discard useful latent work.
A visible-candidate requirement may bias toward tasks that are easy to package as PRs.
Holding production can underutilize A/B if the underlying failure was transient.
records.evaluation_window: Next 4-8 healthy controller cycles after a replacement pull is eventually released.
evaluation_criteria: Any released Tier-2 assignment becomes a visible producer-ready candidate within two healthy D cycles or is explicitly cancelled.
No duplicate replacement PRs are created for the same invisible assignment.
Controller reconciliation/toil declines relative to the preceding three windows.
C/D WIP remains <=2 and useful integration throughput resumes without weakening independent review.

observed_outcomes.observation: At canonical main bebd0a9d2ecc88786af981c0290b594ec76cff31, live PR state contains only deferred PR #70; no P05 candidate exists.
Canonical portfolio already holds new Tier-2 production specifically because the P05 assignment aged without a candidate and this checkpoint was overdue.
The failure is presently best treated as an invisible work-pull/process problem, not evidence that P05 itself is low value.

failures_side_effects: Producer capacity has remained idle for Tier-2 work while the overdue checkpoint blocked replacement allocation.
Repeated controller reconciliation without recording this checkpoint prolonged the hold.
lessons: Finish-before-start must include invisible assignments, not only open PRs.
Do not reissue an aged invisible assignment by default; cancel/reconsider it after the aging threshold.
A process safeguard that requires a checkpoint must record it promptly or it becomes its own source of toil.
After this checkpoint becomes canonical, perform a fresh live-state coherence check before deciding whether P05 still has the highest expected decision delta.
